title: Edge tracing: deferred span flush + multi-protocol propagation adapter
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce tail latency and improve trace completeness for requests entering Redwood via our edge proxy and non-HTTP transports (gRPC streams, raw TCP consumers) by implementing a deferred-span-flush mechanism in the SDK and a lightweight propagation adapter that normalizes context across HTTP/gRPC/TCP boundaries.

Background: We see ~5-10% of requests with missing or truncated spans when requests traverse the edge proxy + internal fan-out. Root cause appears to be: 1) premature span flush at the proxy when downstream routing is async, and 2) inconsistent propagation headers/metadata across transports and load balancers. Current hooks (ENG-4927, ENG-6382) cover most HTTP paths but do not handle long-lived streams or proxy batching.

Approach:
- SDK: Implement "deferred span flush" config that keeps server-side root spans open until explicit drain or timeout (configurable: 50-500ms) to capture downstream async child spans. This will be opt-in per-route with tenant safety guardrails.
- Edge proxy adapter: Add a propagation adapter module that: normalizes traceparent/baggage for HTTP, gRPC (metadata), and custom TCP header encodings; re-injects canonical headers when proxying to internal services; and supports backwards-compatible sampling decisions.
- Compatibility: Build on OpenTelemetry semantics; ensure span IDs and trace IDs are preserved and that baggage size is bounded.
- Metrics/Logging: Emit metrics for deferred-span-duration, deferred-span-drain-count, propagation-drop-rate. Add structured log lines when a span is force-flushed due to timeout.

Trade-offs and safeguards:
- Deferred spans can increase memory/RT cost for long-running requests; enforce a hard cap per-worker and route-level opt-in with tenant quotas.
- Sampling decisions must be respected to avoid amplifying telemetry. If a request was unsampled, deferred flush should not change that.

Success criteria (SLOs):
- Reduce "missing-child-span" alerts by 60% on top-50 services for the next 30 days post-rollout.
- No increase in 95th-percentile memory usage >5% on dedicated edge workers.

Testing and rollout:
- Unit tests: serializers, adapter compatibility matrix (HTTP/gRPC/TCP).
- Integration: e2e test against a lightweight harness that simulates proxy fan-out and gRPC streams.
- Canary rollout: start with internal services (canary tag) -> small customer beta -> global.

Dashboards and alerts:
- New Grafana panels under Observability > Tracing: Deferred Span Duration histogram, Deferred Span Drain Rate, Propagation Drop Rate by route.
- Alerting rules: propagation_drop_rate > 0.5% for 5m (pager) and deferred_span_drain_error_rate > 0.1% (pager).

Artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Deferred+Span+Flush+and+Propagation+Adapter
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/324 (WIP)
- Testing harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability-e2e/tree/feature/deferred-spans

Open questions:
- Default timeout: 100ms is a starting point; ops preference for 50ms to reduce memory pressure.
- Tenant opt-in UX in Console: should be per-route toggle or global per-dedicated-cluster?

Next steps: finalize adapter API, implement SDK config, add metrics hooks, and open PR for proto change in edge-proxy.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Triage: Added to Observability Platform board. Priority P1 due to customer-visible missing spans. Assigned to Marcus Li.
2025-02-18 - Design review: PM (Lina Morales) and Observability lead (Evan Cho) approved deferred flush concept. Ops raised memory cap concern; propose 2-tier cap: route-level and global per-worker.
2025-02-24 - Prototype: initial SDK proof-of-concept implemented. Local load test shows 30% reduction in missing child spans for async fan-out case; memory increased by ~2% at 100ms timeout.
2025-02-28 - PR opened: edge-proxy propagation adapter (WIP) https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/324. Waiting on serialization tests for gRPC metadata case.

2025-03-03 - Security note: Confirmed no additional PII is written to baggage; added max-baggage-size config. Security review flag set to false for now but will re-open if adapter introduces new headers.
2025-03-05 - Blocker: discovered a race on shutdown where worker drain may not flush deferred spans before process exit. Investigating graceful-drain hook in k8s sidecar and SDK signal handler.
